expert_proposals.title: Raise default_statistics_target to sharpen GetUserTweets index selectivity
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=100 leaves histogram/MCV resolution coarse for the skewed tweets.user_id distribution; GetUserTweets (87.9% of terminal capacity, p50 151us, p95 448us) is an Index Scan whose row estimate drives plan choice, and the r002 cache/planner-cost bundle raised TPS but refuted the p95-latency prediction, so the residual bottleneck is estimate quality rather than cache capacity.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal occupancy at 87.9% and is served by an Index Scan; its cost depends on the planner's selectivity estimate for the skewed user_id predicate. default_statistics_target=100 caps histogram buckets and MCV list length, so estimates for heavy-hitter users are coarse and the executor may over-read index/heap pages per call. Raising the target to 400 (within [50,500]) quadruples resolution, tightening selectivity estimates and reducing per-call page touches and p50/p95 latency, freeing terminal capacity for higher successful TPS. This is a distinct mechanism class from the refuted cache-capacity bundle: it targets estimate resolution, not buffer size or cost constants.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Sharper column statistics for tweets.user_id should let the planner pick a tighter index path for GetUserTweets, reducing pages read per call and lowering its p50/p95 latency; plan_evidence root remains Index Scan.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps (>=0.5%) as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy falls.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease; overall p95 flat-to-slightly-down.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Quadruple from 100 to 400 within safe [50,500]; 4x resolution for skewed user_id histograms while keeping ANALYZE cost bounded.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: column statistics resolution for skewed predicate selectivity

predictions.rationale: Higher stats resolution tightens selectivity for skewed user_id, reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call.
Lower GetUserTweets terminal occupancy frees finite client terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
Better estimates reduce worst-case over-reads on heavy-hitter users, trimming the p95 tail.

alternatives.statement: If the residual bottleneck is buffer capacity rather than estimate resolution, raising shared_buffers further (already 65536) would lower GetUserTweets latency; but r002 already tested cache capacity and refuted the p95 prediction, so this is less likely.

If GetUserTweets latency is dominated by WAL sync queueing (wal_wait anomaly, sync_average_ms 0.14), the WAL commit-path bundle would lower InsertTweet latency and raise TPS without changing GetUserTweets p50.

cross_domain_requirements: ANALYZE must run after the reload for new statistics to take effect; executor should trigger ANALYZE on tweets.

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path bundle: buffer capacity, writer cadence, flush batching, group commit, compression
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: wal_buffers=512 (4MB) with wal_writer_delay=200ms and commit_delay=0 forces each committing backend to self-flush; wal_waiting_backends spikes to 2 and wal_sync_time_per_txn=1.16ms dominates the 0.14ms sync average, while wal_compression=off leaves FPI volume (0.000143 FPI/txn) uncompressed.
expert_proposals.mechanism: The WAL commit path is under-provisioned: small wal_buffers plus a 200ms writer cadence means backends frequently find no pre-flushed WAL and must issue their own fsync, producing wal_wait queueing. Enlarging wal_buffers to 2048 (16MB) absorbs bursts; shortening wal_writer_delay to 20ms and lowering wal_writer_flush_after to 0 lets the writer flush promptly so commits find WAL already durable; a small commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 collects concurrent committers into one fsync; wal_compression=on shrinks FPI WAL bytes, reducing write/sync volume. Together these cut per-commit sync frequency and queueing, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
expert_proposals.query_effect: InsertTweet commits (the only WAL-generating path) should complete with fewer self-issued fsyncs; GetUserTweets read latency is unaffected directly but benefits from reduced backend contention on the WAL writer lock.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (0.5-2%) via reduced commit-path queueing and lower WAL volume; primary gain is lower InsertTweet tail latency.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95/p99 decrease; overall p95 roughly unchanged since GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 4MB to 16MB, at safe high bound 2048 (8kB units); absorbs commit bursts without exceeding shared_buffers headroom.
Lower to safe low bound 20ms so the writer flushes WAL before backends arrive; 10x faster cadence.
0 disables forced flush-after, letting the writer flush on its own cadence rather than at 1MB boundaries; safe low bound.
100us collection window is well under the 0.14ms sync average, so it can batch concurrent committers into one fsync without adding net latency; safe range [0,1000].
Lower activation threshold to 2 so group commit engages with the observed 4-6 active backends; safe range [0,20].
Enable to compress full-page images; observed 0.000143 FPI/txn and 4.8 WAL bytes/txn mean FPI dominates WAL volume, so compression reduces write/sync bytes.

predictions.rationale: Larger wal_buffers + faster writer cadence + group commit reduce backends waiting on WAL flush.
Group commit batches multiple committers per fsync, lowering average sync time per commit.
wal_compression=on compresses FPI, reducing WAL bytes per transaction.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity, raising completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: If the bottleneck is purely WAL buffer capacity, raising wal_buffers alone (without writer cadence/group commit changes) would reduce wal_waiting_backends but leave sync_average_ms unchanged.
If FPI volume dominates, wal_compression=on alone would cut wal_bytes_per_txn by >20% while sync_average_ms stays flat.

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path bundle: buffer, writer cadence, flush batch, group commit, compression
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: wal_buffers=512 (4MB) with wal_writer_delay=200ms and commit_delay=0 forces each committing backend to self-fsync; wal_sync_time_per_txn=1.16ms and wal_sync_per_txn=0.0081 show syncs are frequent and unbatched, and wal_waiting_backends spikes to 2 while lock_waiting_backends stays 0.
expert_proposals.mechanism: No SERIALIZABLE retry regime exists (server_retry_ratio=0.0, rollback_ratio=0.0, conflicts_per_txn=0, lock_waiting_backends=0), so predicate-lock knobs are not the lever. The residual anomaly is WAL commit-path queueing: small wal_buffers plus a 200ms writer cadence and zero group-commit window leave each commit to its own fdatasync. Enlarging wal_buffers, shortening wal_writer_delay, raising wal_writer_flush_after, opening a small commit_delay window with a lower commit_siblings threshold, and enabling wal_compression to cut FPI volume should batch syncs, reduce wal_waiting_backends, and free terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Commit-path batching should shorten InsertTweet p99 and reduce WAL wait stalls; read-heavy GetUserTweets is unaffected except through freed terminal capacity.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (0.5-2%) from reduced commit-path queueing and freed terminal capacity.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p99 decreases; GetUserTweets p50 roughly unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 4MB to 16MB, at safe high bound 2048 (8kB units); ample RAM headroom.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: WAL buffering capacity to absorb commit bursts

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reduce from 200ms to 50ms, within safe [20,500]; faster writer wake-up flushes WAL sooner.
Double flush batch from 128 to 256 (8kB units), within safe [0,1024]; larger batches reduce sync frequency.
Open a 100us group-commit window, within safe [0,1000]; small enough to avoid added latency while collecting siblings.
Lower activation threshold from 5 to 2, within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 2 siblings reliably triggers group commit.
Enable to compress full-page images; wal_fpi_per_txn=1.4e-4 shows FPI volume exists and compression reduces WAL bytes per commit.

predictions.rationale: Larger WAL buffers plus shorter writer cadence and group-commit window batch syncs, lowering peak WAL waiters.
Group commit amortizes fdatasync across siblings, reducing per-transaction sync time.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity for the dominant GetUserTweets class.

alternatives.statement: If the residual tail is SIRead lock bookkeeping rather than WAL, tightening max_pred_locks_per_page/relation would lower GetUserTweets p99; but lock_waiting_backends=0 and retry_ratio=0 make this unlikely.
If WAL sync latency is already negligible (0.14ms), the bundle yields no measurable TPS change and wal_waiting_backends stays at 0 median.
